{{about|the Mexican mathematician|the Mexican politician|Martha Partida Guzmán}}
{{Family name hatnote|Guzmán|Partida|lang=Spanish}}
'''Martha Dolores Guzmán Partida''' is a Mexican mathematician specializing in [[functional analysis]], including [[Fourier analysis]], [[harmonic analysis]], and the theory of [[Distribution (mathematics)|distributions]]. She is a professor of mathematics at the [[Universidad de Sonora]].{{r|ingresan|uson}}

==Education==
Guzmán Partida was an undergraduate at the [[Meritorious Autonomous University of Puebla]].{{r|misc}} She completed her doctorate in 1995 at the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]]. Her dissertation, ''Hardy Spaces of Conjugates Temperatures'', was supervised by Salvador Pérez Esteva.{{r|mg}}

==Recognition==
Guzmán was elected to the [[Mexican Academy of Sciences]] in 2013.{{r|ingresan|amc}}

== Selected publications ==
* Alvarez, J; Lakey, J.; Guzmán–Partida, Martha. "Spaces of bounded lambda–central mean oscillation, Morrey spaces, and lambda–central Carleson measures." ''Collectanea Mathematica'', 51 (1), 2000, pp. 1–47.
* Alvarez, J; Guzmán–Partida, Martha; Pérez–Esteva, S. "Harmonic extensions of distributions." ''Mathematische Nachrichten'', 280 (13–14), 2007, pp.1443–1466. 
* Alvarez, J; Guzmán–Partida, Martha; Skórnik, U. "S'–convolvability with the Poisson kernel in the Euclidean case and the product domain case." ''Studia Mathematica'', 2 (156), 2003, pp.143–163.
